conclusion: A payload version can evolve independently from the v1 envelope, but capability selection must remain explicit and dependency-closed: generic dispatch requires topology, queue, memory, signal, and code-object transport capabilities.
decision: Keep framing major/minor at 1.0, add payload major/minor 2.0 and capability bit 8, reserve message types 18/19/20, and reject partial or offered-only generic capability selections.
invalidated_assumptions: A new payload family can silently reuse v1 dispatch IDs or reinterpret A1 code-object records.
An advertised generic capability is safe without queue, memory, signal, and code-object ownership dependencies.
observation: The runtime codec validates the existing envelope and CRC, a distinct payload version, bit-8 dependency closure, and non-overlapping reserved record IDs while preserving all earlier CTest behavior.
question_or_symptom: How can a generic launch wire be introduced without changing byte-level v1 behavior or allowing a partially negotiated capability?
